reason: I'll build the artery first: the picture shows the lining fitting inside its strong, elastic wall.
expectation: I expect a lined artery that can stretch and spring back as blood flows through it.

alternatives.reason: The capillaries and nearby cells also clearly fit the exchange goal, but I'll start with the route out from the heart.

effect: The artery is lined and carries blood away from the heart, completing the first goal.
reaction: The result matched the picture I expected.
reason: I'll bring the capillaries near body cells to work on the exchange goal.
expectation: I expect thin capillary walls to put blood close enough to cells for materials to move between them.

alternatives.reason: Lining the vein also supports a goal, but I'll follow the route outward to the exchange vessels first.

effect: The capillary bed shows oxygen and nutrients moving to cells and carbon dioxide moving into blood, while blood cells stay inside.
reaction: The thin walls make the exchange easier to picture.
reason: I'll line the venous wall to start the remaining return-route goal.
expectation: I expect a lined vein, probably still needing the one-way valve flaps.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the arteries to the capillary bed follows the blood's route, but I want to prepare the return route first.

effect: The lined veins point back toward the heart, but still need valves for the return-route goal.
reaction: The result matched what I expected.
reason: I'll add the valve flaps to complete the return route.
expectation: I expect veins with flaps that open for blood moving toward the heart and close against backward flow.

alternatives.reason: Joining arteries to the capillary bed also follows the route, but I'll finish the veins first.

effect: The valves complete the return route, and the picture shows how a contracting muscle helps move blood forward. The next goal is to join the routes.
reaction: The muscle squeezing the vein was a useful detail I hadn't expected.
reason: I'll connect the arteries to the capillary bed as the only offered combination toward joining the routes.
expectation: I expect a route from the arteries into the capillaries, probably still needing the veins connected.

effect: The arteries now branch into the capillaries, leaving the return side open for the veins.
reaction: The branching picture makes the route clear.
reason: I'll connect the venous return to join all three routes; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a connected route through arteries, capillaries and veins back toward the heart.

effect: The final connection completed the route from the heart through arteries and capillaries and back through veins.
reaction: The continuous route made the three vessel jobs easy to put together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the capillary bed was most worthwhile because it showed what moves between blood and body cells, and that blood cells stay inside.

leastWorthwhile.text: Lining the vein felt least interesting because it closely resembled lining the artery, though it had a clear purpose.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the picture to show a contracting muscle squeezing a vein to help blood move forward through the valves.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary; the pictures and goals explained why the parts belonged together, although the last two combinations were the only ones offered.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: seeing the separate vessel jobs become one route was satisfying, and I'd be curious how it connects to the heart.
